evidence: src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) injects the persistence service
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts:14: log() does `const prisma = new PrismaClient();`, ignoring the injected this.prisma
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts:15: `await prisma.payrollAudit.create({...})` writes through the ad-hoc PrismaClient
src/business/services/PayrollAuditService.ts:19: trail() uses this.prisma.payrollAudit.findMany, the injected port, so the class reaches persistence in two different ways
src/business/services/PayrollService.ts: persistence goes only through the injected EmployeeRepository and TimesheetRepository (byId, create, approve, active, forWeek)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: PayrollAuditService is given an injected PrismaService and uses it in trail(). But log() creates its own `new PrismaClient()` from @prisma/client and calls payrollAudit.create on it. This bypasses the module's own injected persistence port, so the same class reaches the database in two different ways, and log() opens a fresh, unmanaged connection. That is the 'reaches persistence around the module's own repository or port' failure, so the line 14–15 flags are confirmed. The line-19 flag (findMany through this.prisma) uses the injected port and is not a bypass in itself. PayrollService only uses its injected EmployeeRepository and TimesheetRepository and the domain model types, and I found no rule copied between the two files. A lesser inconsistency, not counted as a violation: PayrollService uses domain repositories, while PayrollAuditService uses the raw Prisma service with no audit repository.

violations.message: PayrollAuditService.log creates `new PrismaClient()` from @prisma/client and calls payrollAudit.create directly. This bypasses the module's injected PrismaService (this.prisma), which trail() uses, so persistence is reached around the class's own port and through an unmanaged client.
